claude.country: Unknown (public datasets from tuberculosis screening programs)
models_evaluated: multimodal generative AI radiology report model

links.outcome: Reader accuracy for TB detection with versus without AI-generated reports
links.effect: Reader 1 accuracy 93.4% without vs 94.1% with AI reports (p=.47); reader 2 91.3% vs 93.5% (p=.03). Localization did not significantly change for either reader.
links.quote: Accuracy was significantly lower for AI-generated reports than for both readers alone (p < .001), but significantly higher with than without AI-generated reports for one reader (reader 1: p = .47; reader 2: p = .03).

links.outcome: Standalone AI report accuracy versus radiologists alone on same radiographs
links.effect: AI report accuracy 90.8% vs reader 1 93.4% and reader 2 91.3%; accuracy significantly lower than both readers (p<.001); localization 63.3% vs 79.8% and 77.9%.
links.quote: Localization performance was significantly lower (p < .001) for AI-generated reports (63.3%) than for reader 1 (79.8%) and reader 2 (77.9%) without AI-generated reports and did not significantly change for either reader with AI-generated reports (reader 1: 78.7%, p = .71; reader 2: 81.5%, p = .23).

links.outcome: Radiologist acceptance of AI-generated reports without modification, by normal/abnormal status
links.effect: Reader 1 accepted 91.7% of normal and 52.4% of abnormal reports; reader 2 accepted 83.2% and 37.0%, showing many abnormal reports needed modification.
links.quote: Among normal and abnormal radiographs, reader 1 accepted 91.7% and 52.4%, whereas reader 2 accepted 83.2% and 37.0%, respectively, of AI-generated reports.

links.effect: AI report accuracy was 90.8%; reader-with-AI accuracies were 94.1% and 93.5%.
links.quote: For detection of tuberculosis-related abnormalities, sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy were 95.2%, 86.7%, and 90.8% for AI-generated reports; 93.1%, 93.6%, and 93.4% for reader 1 without AI-generated reports; 93.1%, 95.0%, and 94.1% for reader 1 with AI-generated reports; 95.8%, 87.2%, and 91.3% for reader 2 without AI-generated reports; and 95.8%, 91.5%, and 93.5% for reader 2 with AI-generated reports.

links.outcome: reader detection accuracy with versus without AI
links.effect: Detection accuracy was significantly higher with AI for one reader (reader 1: p = .47; reader 2: p = .03).
links.quote: Accuracy was significantly lower for AI-generated reports than for both readers alone (p < .001), but significantly higher with than without AI-generated reports for one reader (reader 1: p = .47; reader 2: p = .03).

links.effect: AI-generated report accuracy was significantly lower than both readers alone (p < .001).
links.quote: Accuracy was significantly lower for AI-generated reports than for both readers alone (p < .001), but significantly higher with than without AI-generated reports for one reader (reader 1: p = .47; reader 2: p = .03).

links.effect: AI localization was 63.3%, below reader 1 79.8% and reader 2 77.9% without AI (p < .001).
links.quote: Localization performance was significantly lower (p < .001) for AI-generated reports (63.3%) than for reader 1 (79.8%) and reader 2 (77.9%) without AI-generated reports and did not significantly change for either reader with AI-generated reports (reader 1: 78.7%, p = .71; reader 2: 81.5%, p = .23).

links.outcome: acceptance of AI-generated reports without modification
links.effect: Reader 1 accepted 91.7% of normal and 52.4% of abnormal reports; reader 2 accepted 83.2% of normal and 37.0% of abnormal reports without modification.
links.quote: Among normal and abnormal radiographs, reader 1 accepted 91.7% and 52.4%, whereas reader 2 accepted 83.2% and 37.0%, respectively, of AI-generated reports.

screen.reason: Empirical reader study comparing diagnostic accuracy of radiologists reviewing chest radiographs with versus without assistance from a multimodal generative AI model generating radiology reports.
